key_insight: ReLMem learns a fixed-size recurrent patient memory that updates with each new EHR visit, aiming to preserve useful history without rereading the full record.
clinical_relevance: This could make longitudinal medication prediction more efficient for large EHR timelines by cutting storage and compute while keeping performance close to full-history models.
method: Uses lightweight compression adapters on a frozen LLM to update memory from the previous state plus the incoming visit
Applies intermediate supervision to match attention outputs from compressed memory and full history under the same query
Adds final prediction supervision with cross-entropy on the downstream task
evidence_signal: On EHR-based medication prediction, ReLMem reduced retained historical storage by 97.1% and improved macro-/micro-F1 by 4.66 and 4.75 points over the strongest compressed-memory baseline, while approaching full-history performance.
watch_item: Results are task-specific and depend on the chosen memory budget, so performance may vary when adapted to other EHR tasks or clinical settings.
paper_title: ReLMem: Learning Recurrent Memory for Longitudinal EHR Modeling
